questions.topic: Introduction to Fabrication and Welding Practice
questions.stem: Fabrication, in metal work, is best described as
options: melting iron ore in a blast furnace
making structures and products by cutting, bending and joining metal parts
mining metal ores from the ground
questions.explanation: Fabrication converts stock metal into products through cutting, forming and assembly (often by welding).

questions.topic: Safety Precautions in Welding and Fabrication Workshop
questions.stem: An arc welder must wear a helmet fitted with a dark filter lens mainly to protect the eyes from
options: intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation from the arc
questions.explanation: Arc radiation causes "arc eye" and retinal burns; the filter lens absorbs UV and IR.

questions.topic: Safety Precautions in Welding and Fabrication Workshop
questions.stem: Welding inside a closed metal tank that previously held petrol is dangerous mainly because
options: the tank is too heavy to move
steel cannot be welded when cold
the electrode will not strike an arc
petrol vapour remaining in the tank can explode
questions.explanation: Residual flammable vapour must be removed by cleaning/purging and the tank tested before any hot work.

questions.stem: In a well-planned fabrication and welding workshop, arc welding bays should be
options: placed next to the paint store
separated by screens and fitted with fume extraction
located in the middle of the main gangway
left unventilated to keep heat in
questions.explanation: Screens protect others from arc flash; extraction removes fumes; flammables must be kept away.

questions.stem: On a welding symbol, a small circle drawn where the arrow joins the reference line means
questions.explanation: The circle is the "weld all round" symbol; a flag denotes a field (site) weld.

questions.stem: A welder's hand is burnt by touching hot metal. The correct immediate first aid is to
options: apply engine oil to the burn
cool the burn under cool running water for at least 10 minutes
questions.explanation: Cool running water reduces tissue damage and pain; oils and bursting blisters increase infection risk.

questions.stem: Which of these metals is FERROUS?
questions.explanation: Ferrous metals are iron-based; copper, zinc and tin are non-ferrous.

questions.stem: The property of a metal that allows it to be drawn out into a thin wire is
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be stretched (drawn) under tension; malleability is shaping by hammering or rolling.

questions.stem: A metal that breaks suddenly with little or no bending when struck, such as grey cast iron, is described as
questions.explanation: Brittle materials fracture without significant plastic deformation; tough materials absorb energy before breaking.

questions.stem: On the Standard Wire Gauge (SWG) system for sheet metal, as the gauge number increases, the sheet becomes
questions.explanation: Higher gauge numbers indicate thinner sheet, e.g. 24 SWG is thinner than 16 SWG.

questions.topic: Selection of Suitable Metals for Specific Jobs
questions.stem: Which metal is most suitable for making a light, corrosion-resistant boat hull or ladder?
questions.explanation: Aluminium alloys are light, strong for their weight and resist corrosion; cast iron is heavy and brittle.

questions.stem: Heating steel above its upper critical temperature and allowing it to cool in still air to refine the grain is
questions.explanation: Normalising cools in still air; annealing cools slowly in the furnace; hardening quenches rapidly.

questions.stem: The tool used to remove slag from a completed arc weld is the
questions.explanation: The chipping hammer knocks off the slag coating; a wire brush then cleans the weld.

questions.topic: Equipment Set-up for Gas and Arc Welding and Fabrication
questions.stem: When setting up oxy-acetylene equipment, the cylinder valves should be opened
options: slowly, with the regulator adjusting screws released and standing to one side of the gauges
quickly to full open with the adjusting screws tight
only after the torch is lit
with oil on the threads for smooth opening
questions.explanation: Slow opening against released regulators prevents gauge damage and adiabatic heating; oil must never be used on oxygen fittings.

questions.stem: A clamping device shaped like the letter G, used to hold work to a bench or two parts together during tack welding, is the
questions.explanation: G-clamps (C-clamps) hold workpieces; tongs are used in forging.

questions.topic: Measuring Instruments, Marking Out and Cutting Tools
questions.stem: Which tool is used to mark a line parallel to the edge of a metal plate?
questions.explanation: Odd-leg callipers scribe lines parallel to an edge; the centre punch marks centres for drilling.

questions.topic: Parts and Accessories for Gas and Arc Welding
questions.stem: In arc welding, the part that connects the return (work) cable firmly to the workpiece is the
questions.explanation: The work clamp completes the circuit; the electrode holder grips the electrode.

questions.stem: Oxygen regulators and cylinder fittings must never be lubricated with oil or grease because
options: oil makes the gauges read wrongly
oil can ignite violently in contact with high-pressure oxygen
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons can spontaneously ignite in pure pressurised oxygen, causing fire or explosion.

questions.topic: Preparation of Acetylene Gas from Carbide
questions.stem: Calcium carbide reacts with water: CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. What mass of acetylene can be obtained from 1.28 kg of pure calcium carbide? (CaC2 = 64, C2H2 = 26)
questions.explanation: 1 mol CaC2 (64 g) gives 1 mol C2H2 (26 g): 1.28 x 26/64 = 0.52 kg.

questions.stem: The flux coating on a metal-arc electrode
options: produces a shielding gas and slag that protect the molten weld from the air
questions.explanation: The coating stabilises the arc, shields the weld pool with gas and slag, and may add alloying elements.

questions.topic: Equipment for Fault Detection and Trouble Shooting
questions.stem: A non-destructive test in which a coloured liquid is applied to a weld, wiped off and a developer used to reveal surface cracks is the
questions.explanation: Dye penetrant reveals surface-breaking flaws without damaging the part; bend, nick-break and tensile tests are destructive.

questions.stem: In manual metal-arc welding, the heat for melting the metal is produced by
options: an electric arc between the electrode and the workpiece
questions.explanation: MMA uses the arc; oxy-acetylene welding uses a gas flame.

questions.stem: The correct sequence in a typical sheet metal fabrication job is
options: finishing, joining, cutting, marking out, forming
joining, marking out, finishing, cutting, forming
forming, finishing, marking out, joining, cutting
marking out, cutting, forming, joining, finishing
questions.explanation: The blank is marked and cut, then bent/formed, assembled and finally finished.

questions.stem: Two plates placed at right angles to form a T shape and welded with fillet welds form a
questions.explanation: A tee joint has one plate perpendicular to the other; a butt joint has plates edge to edge in the same plane.

questions.stem: Before marking out on bright mild steel, the surface is coated with marking blue in order to
options: prevent the steel from rusting permanently
questions.explanation: Marking blue (layout dye) gives a contrasting background so scribed lines show clearly.

questions.stem: A template is used in fabrication mainly to
options: reproduce the same shape accurately and quickly on many workpieces
test the hardness of a weld
questions.explanation: Templates save marking-out time and ensure identical parts in batch work.

questions.stem: In oxy-acetylene welding, the rightward (backhand) technique is preferred to the leftward technique for steel plate
options: thicker than about 5 mm, because it gives better penetration and uses less gas
thinner than 1 mm, because it gives a neater ripple
of any thickness when welding aluminium
questions.explanation: Rightward welding directs the flame onto the deposited metal, giving faster welding of thick plate; leftward suits thin sheet.

questions.stem: Using the rule that the allowance for a wired edge is 2.5 times the wire diameter, the allowance needed to wire the edge of a tray with 3 mm wire is
questions.explanation: Allowance = 2.5 x 3 = 7.5 mm, enough metal to wrap round the wire.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a TEMPORARY fastener?
questions.explanation: Bolts and nuts can be removed without damage; rivets, welds and solder joints are permanent.

questions.topic: Rivets, Bolts and Nuts, and Screws
questions.stem: Two 5 mm plates are to be joined with 6 mm diameter snap-head rivets. Allowing 1.5 times the diameter to form the head, the length of each rivet should be
In forging, the tool used to hold hot metal while it is being hammered is the pair of
questions.explanation: Smith's tongs grip hot work safely; dividers and callipers are measuring/marking tools.

questions.stem: The forging operation that increases the cross-section of a bar while reducing its length is
questions.explanation: Upsetting (jumping up) thickens the bar by hammering on its end; drawing down does the opposite.

questions.topic: Preparation of Welding Surfaces and Edges
questions.stem: A single-V butt preparation is used on thicker plates mainly to
options: reduce the amount of cleaning needed
allow the weld to penetrate the full thickness of the joint
questions.explanation: Bevelling the edges gives access for the arc or flame to fuse the root and full thickness.

questions.stem: A groove melted into the parent metal along the edge of a weld and left unfilled is
questions.explanation: Undercut is usually caused by excessive current, wrong electrode angle or too fast travel.

questions.stem: Which of these makes a welding environment UNSAFE?
options: Oil and grease on the floor near the welding bay
questions.explanation: Slippery, flammable oil on the floor creates both slip and fire hazards.

questions.topic: Surface Furnishing for Fabrication and Welding
questions.stem: Coating fabricated steel with zinc by dipping it in a bath of molten zinc is called
questions.explanation: Galvanising protects steel from rust; anodising is an oxide treatment for aluminium.

questions.stem: To make the cylindrical body of a charcoal stove 150 mm in diameter, the length of the sheet-metal blank, ignoring seam allowance, is about (pi = 3.142)
questions.explanation: Blank length = circumference = pi x d = 3.142 x 150 = 471.2 mm (seam allowance added separately).

questions.stem: A person who starts and manages a welding business, taking the financial risk in the hope of profit, is a(n)
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur takes the risk of starting and running a business; employees work for wages.

questions.stem: Compared with a large-scale enterprise, a small-scale welding enterprise usually has
options: fewer employees, lower capital and simpler management
shares quoted on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Small-scale enterprises have few workers, small capital and are usually owner-managed.

questions.topic: Factors for Setting up a Workshop
questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important when choosing a site for a welding workshop in Onitsha?
options: Availability of reliable electric power and access to market
Nearness to a primary school playground
questions.explanation: Arc welding depends on power, and the workshop must be accessible to customers and suppliers.

questions.topic: Safety Precautions in Welding and Fabrication Workshop
questions.stem:
(a) State four causes of accidents in a welding and fabrication workshop. [4 marks]
(b) List four items of protective wear used by welders and state what each protects. [8 marks]
(c) State three ways of preventing environmental pollution from welding fumes. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: carelessness/horseplay; faulty equipment or damaged cables; poor ventilation; flammable materials near welding; untidy floor/oil spills; not wearing protective wear; ignorance of safety rules; leaking gas cylinders
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: welding helmet/shield with filter lens - eyes and face from arc radiation and spatter; gas welding goggles - eyes from glare and sparks; leather gloves/gauntlets - hands from heat, sparks and shock; leather apron - body from sparks and spatter; safety boots - feet from falling objects and hot metal; ear protectors - ears from noise; respirator - lungs from fumes
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: local fume extraction; general ventilation; use of low-fume electrodes/processes; welding outdoors where possible; cleaning paint/coatings off before welding; proper disposal of waste
questions.explanation: Causes: carelessness, faulty equipment, poor ventilation, flammables, untidy floors, no PPE. PPE: helmet (eyes/face from arc), goggles, gloves (hands), apron (body), boots (feet), ear protectors, respirator. Pollution control: fume extraction, ventilation, low-fume consumables, cleaning surfaces, proper waste disposal.

questions.topic: Equipment Set-up for Gas and Arc Welding and Fabrication
questions.stem:
(a) List six items of equipment needed for oxy-acetylene welding. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for setting up and lighting an oxy-acetylene welding torch. [6 marks]
(c) State three items of equipment for manual metal-arc welding. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) Any six, 1 mark each: oxygen cylinder; acetylene cylinder; oxygen regulator; acetylene regulator; hoses (blue and red); flashback arrestors/check valves; blowpipe/torch; nozzles; spark lighter; goggles; cylinder trolley
6 marks: (b) 1 mark each: secure cylinders upright on trolley and crack valves to blow out dirt; fit regulators (right-hand thread oxygen, left-hand acetylene) and arrestors; connect hoses and blowpipe with correct nozzle; open cylinder valves slowly and set working pressures; check all joints for leaks with soapy water; open acetylene valve slightly, light with spark lighter, then add oxygen to obtain a neutral flame
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: welding transformer/generator/inverter; electrode holder; earth (work) clamp and cables; electrodes; helmet with filter lens; chipping hammer and wire brush
questions.explanation: Gas set: cylinders, regulators, hoses, arrestors, blowpipe, nozzles, lighter, goggles. Set up: secure and crack cylinders, fit regulators and arrestors, connect hoses and torch, set pressures, leak test, light acetylene with a spark lighter then add oxygen for a neutral flame. MMA: power source, electrode holder, work clamp and cables, electrodes, helmet.

questions.topic: Preparation of Acetylene Gas from Carbide
questions.stem:
(a) Write a balanced equation for the production of acetylene from calcium carbide. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate, for 2 kg of pure calcium carbide reacting completely with water: (i) the mass of acetylene produced (ii) the volume of acetylene at s.t.p. (Ca = 40, C = 12, H = 1; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 litres). [6 marks]
(c) State three safety precautions in handling calcium carbide and acetylene. [3 marks]
(d) Why is acetylene in cylinders dissolved in acetone? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2 (correct formulae 2, balancing 1)
1 mark: (b) Molar masses: CaC2 = 40 + 24 = 64 g/mol; C2H2 = 24 + 2 = 26 g/mol
2 marks: (b)(i) Mass of C2H2 = 2000 x 26/64 = 812.5 g (0.8125 kg)
3 marks: (b)(ii) Moles of CaC2 = 2000/64 = 31.25 mol = moles of C2H2; volume = 31.25 x 22.4 = 700 litres (0.7 m^3)
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: store carbide in sealed, dry, labelled containers away from water; no naked flames/smoking near carbide and generators; ventilate generator area; never use copper fittings with acetylene (explosive acetylides); do not exceed about 1 bar free acetylene pressure; dispose of lime residue safely
3 marks: (d) Free acetylene is unstable and can decompose explosively above about 1 bar (1); acetone dissolves large volumes of acetylene (1); the porous mass and acetone allow safe storage at higher cylinder pressure (1)
questions.explanation: CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2. From 2.0 kg: 812.5 g of acetylene, 31.25 mol, 700 litres at s.t.p. Keep carbide dry and sealed, no flames, ventilate, avoid copper, keep pressure low. Acetone in a porous mass stores acetylene safely because free acetylene is unstable above about 1 bar.

questions.topic: Preparation of Welding Surfaces and Edges
questions.stem:
(a) State four methods of cleaning metal surfaces before welding. [4 marks]
(b) Describe, with reasons, the edge preparation for (i) a square butt joint (ii) a single-V butt joint (iii) a double-V butt joint. [9 marks]
(c) Why is a welded joint oiled or painted after cleaning? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: wire brushing; grinding; filing; scraping; emery cloth; degreasing with solvent; pickling
3 marks: (b)(i) Square butt: edges left square and placed with a small gap; used for thin plate where full penetration is possible without bevelling
3 marks: (b)(ii) Single-V: one edge or both edges bevelled to give an included angle of about 60-70 degrees with a root face and gap; used for medium-thickness plate to give full penetration from one side
3 marks: (b)(iii) Double-V: both edges bevelled from both sides; used for thick plate, needs less filler and reduces distortion because welding is balanced on both sides
2 marks: (c) To protect the cleaned/welded metal from rusting and corrosion until it is finished or painted
questions.explanation: Clean by wire brush, grinder, file, scraper, emery cloth or degreasing. Square butt for thin plate; single-V (60-70 degrees included) for medium plate to get full penetration; double-V for thick plate, saving filler and balancing distortion. Oiling/painting prevents rust.

questions.stem: For each of the following weld defects, state one cause and one remedy: (a) porosity (b) undercut (c) slag inclusion (d) lack of penetration (e) excessive spatter. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Porosity: cause - damp electrodes, contaminated surface (rust, oil, paint) or long arc (2 marks for description/cause); remedy - dry electrodes, clean surface, correct arc length (1)
3 marks: (b) Undercut: cause - excessive current, wrong electrode angle, too fast travel (2); remedy - reduce current, correct angle and speed (1)
3 marks: (c) Slag inclusion: cause - inadequate cleaning of slag between runs, wrong angle (2); remedy - chip and brush thoroughly between runs, correct technique (1)
3 marks: (d) Lack of penetration: cause - too low current, too fast travel, small root gap or wrong preparation (2); remedy - increase current, correct gap/bevel, slower travel (1)
3 marks: (e) Excessive spatter: cause - current too high, arc too long, damp electrodes (2); remedy - reduce current, keep short arc, dry electrodes (1)
questions.explanation: Porosity from damp electrodes or dirty surfaces - dry and clean. Undercut from high current or wrong angle - reduce current, correct angle. Slag inclusion from poor inter-run cleaning - clean thoroughly. Lack of penetration from low current or poor preparation - raise current, correct gap. Spatter from high current or long arc - reduce current, short arc.

questions.stem:
(a) Define forging. [2 marks]
(b) Name four forging tools and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(c) Describe the steps in forging an eye at the end of a mild steel bar. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Shaping of metal, usually heated to a plastic state, by hammering or pressing
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: forge/furnace - heats the metal; anvil - supports work during hammering; tongs - hold hot metal; swages - finish round sections; fullers - make grooves/spread metal; flatters - smooth flat surfaces; hardy - cuts hot metal; sledge/hand hammer - strikes the metal
5 marks: (c) 1 mark each: heat the end of the bar to bright red/yellow heat; draw down/taper the end if required; bend the end over the beak (horn) of the anvil, working progressively; close the eye round a mandrel/bar of the correct size; reheat as needed, true up and cool slowly
questions.explanation: Forging shapes heated metal by hammering. Tools: forge, anvil, tongs, swages, fullers, flatters, hardy, hammers. To form an eye: heat, taper, bend progressively over the anvil horn, close round a mandrel, true up and cool.
